title: What Is an ADT Feed in Healthcare? (July 2026)
summary: What is an ADT feed? Learn how HL7 v2 admission, discharge, and transfer notifications work, CMS requirements, and how ADT data drives care coordination.
body_text: ADT data moves fast and shows up across a range of healthcare workflows, so it's worth understanding exactly how it works. At its core, an ADT feed is a stream of real-time notifications that tells connected systems whenever a patient is admitted, discharged, or transferred. If you're building workflows on top of this data or just trying to make sense of it, here's what you need to know. TLDR: ADT in healthcare tracks patient admissions, discharges, and transfers via real-time HL7 v2 messages sent to billing, care, and admin systems. An ADT feed is a live notification stream, not a database. CMS requires hospitals to make a reasonable effort to send ADT notifications to a patient’s primary care physician and other identified treating clinicians at the time of admission, discharge, or transfer ( 42 CFR § 482.24(d)(5) ). ADT alerts provide limited clinical detail: they typically lack lab results, medication details, or care plans, and offer no historical record. Feed quality also varies widely by hospital and EHR vendor.Metriport's real-time notifications alert care teams the moment an ADT event occurs, and can be paired with a network query to pull the discharge summary and other transition documents into the patient's record. What ADT Means in Healthcare ADT stands for Admission, Discharge, and Transfer. Every time a patient enters a hospital, leaves one, or moves between care settings, an ADT is recorded and broadcast to connected systems. Think of it as the hospital's running log of patient movement. A patient arrives at the emergency department, gets admitted to a med-surg unit, transfers to the ICU, and eventually discharges home. Each step generates an ADT with timestamps, patient demographics, location data, and attending provider details. That event then flows, in real time, to billing systems, care teams, and any external partners subscribed to the feed. These records feed downstream workflows across the health system, including bed management, care coordination, and regulatory reporting, giving staff a shared, up-to-date view of where each patient is and what stage of care they are in. How ADT Events Are Triggered and Transmitted A registration clerk admitting a patient, a nurse transferring them to the ICU, or a discharge planner finalizing paperwork all trigger a discrete HL7 message. That message gets routed through the facility's ADT system. These messages travel over interfaces built on HL7 v2 , a widely deployed legacy messaging standard used by U.S. hospitals. Each message carries a structured payload: patient identifiers, event type codes, timestamps, and location details that downstream systems parse and act on automatically. HL7 v2 vs. FHIR for ADT Messages ADT notifications are almost exclusively sent using HL7 v2. It has been the established clinical messaging standard since the 1980s and is widely used by hospitals to broadcast patient movements to downstream systems such as pharmacy, billing, and HIE networks. FHIR, the federal standard for APIs and patient data access, is capable of representing ADT workflows but its adoption for ADT feeds is still growing. Because most hospital infrastructure is built on HL7 v2, modern systems typically translate traditional HL7 v2 ADT feeds into FHIR formats using middleware. Common ADT Event Types and HL7 Message Codes Each ADT event code is mapped to a discrete clinical trigger, and a handful of message types account for the majority of these event codes. The Most Common ADT Message Types Code Event Trigger A01 Admit/Visit Notification Patient is admitted to inpatient care A02 Transfer a Patient Patient moves to a different unit or bed A03 Discharge/End Visit Patient is discharged or the visit closes A04 Register a Patient Patient registers for an outpatient or ED visit A08 Update Patient Information Demographics or insurance details change A11 Cancel Admit An admission event is reversed A13 Cancel Discharge A discharge event is reversed ‍ The cancel events (A11 and A13) are frequently overlooked but matter for downstream accuracy, since any system acting on an A01 or A03 needs to know if that event is later reversed. ‍ What Data Lives Inside an ADT Feed Each ADT message packages a snapshot of the patient's current state at the moment the event fires. The core fields present in most messages include: Patient demographics: name, date of birth, and gender Visit information: admission and discharge timestamps, visit identifiers, and encounter status Diagnosis: a diagnosis code and description tied to the encounter Patient location: facility name, and for transfers, the source and destination unit or department Attending physician: name and credentials One distinction worth drawing clearly: an ADT feed is a notification stream, not a database. Each message represents a point-in-time event pushed to subscribers as it happens. A static ADT database, by contrast, is a record store built from those accumulated events over time. The feed tells you something just changed; the database tells you the full history of changes. How ADT Systems Improve Hospital Operations Real-time ADT data gives hospitals a clearer picture of patient flow, which directly affects staffing, bed allocation, and discharge planning. When a patient is admitted, transferred, or discharged, that event triggers downstream coordination across nursing, housekeeping, billing, and care management teams. Without timely ADT feeds, these handoffs rely on manual communication that slows response times and creates gaps in care. ADT Feeds and Care Coordination Across Settings When a patient moves between care settings, that transition is one of the highest-risk moments in their care journey. ADT feeds give care coordinators, health plans, digital health services, and post-acute providers real-time visibility into those moments, so follow-up can happen before gaps form. For example, when a patient is discharged from a hospital, a payer receiving that ADT alert can trigger an outreach workflow within hours instead of days. Community health workers, care managers, and primary care teams can all act on the same event simultaneously. ADT Data and Value-Based Care Value-based care models like ACOs and bundled payment arrangements tie reimbursements to outcomes, and ADT data is one of the few real-time signals available to act on. When a patient is admitted to an outside facility, a timely ADT notification gives care managers a window to intervene before a gap in care widens into a costly complication. CMS Requirements for ADT Notifications The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services issued a rule ( 42 CFR § 482.24(d) ) requiring hospitals to send ADT notifications to a patient's primary care provider and other treating clinicians at the time of admission or registration, and immediately prior to or at the time of discharge or transfer. (The obligation falls on the hospital to send these notifications; there is no corresponding requirement that the receiving provider monitor or act on them.) Hospitals that fail to meet this requirement risk losing Medicare and Medicaid participation. The rule applies to most Medicare-participating hospitals, pushing health systems to invest in reliable ADT data infrastructure to stay compliant. For a detailed breakdown, see the CMS ADT notification requirements FAQ . Limitations and Challenges of ADT Data ADT feeds have real constraints that teams should account for before building workflows around them. ADT data is administrative by design: it typically excludes vitals, imaging results, physician notes, and problem/allergy lists, the clinical context needed to understand what actually happened during the visit. Feed quality varies by hospital and EHR vendor, meaning missing fields, inconsistent formatting, and duplicate messages are common. Interoperability gaps persist across health systems, making it harder to align patient records, including ADTs, across organizations. HIPAA compliance requirements add governance overhead for any team receiving or storing ADT data. How Metriport Uses ADT Data for Real-Time Patient Monitoring Metriport's ADT monitoring connects to feeds from Bamboo Health and state and regional HIEs , delivering real-time admission, discharge, and transfer notifications across the US healthcare system. What separates this from a standard alert feed is what happens immediately after the ADT fires: Metriport ties the alert to a Patient Encounter Bundle with the patient, encounter, and diagnosis data, and can trigger a network query to pull the discharge summary, medication list, and other transition documents into the patient's full longitudinal record. Because the alert is tied directly to the encounter data and can pull in the fuller record, care teams can act during an encounter instead of learning about the admission days later through a claims file. For value-based care organizations managing attributed populations, that window is where readmissions get prevented and transitional care management billing gets captured. FAQ What is an ADT feed in healthcare and how does it differ from an ADT database? An ADT feed is a real-time notification stream that pushes a message every time a patient is admitted, discharged, or transferred. An ADT database is a static record store built from those accumulated events over time; the feed tells you something just changed, while the database holds the full history of changes. What HL7 message types should I know for hospital ADT data? The seven message types that cover most real-world ADT traffic are A01 (admit), A02 (transfer), A03 (discharge), A04 (register), A08 (update demographics), A11 (cancel admit), and A13 (cancel discharge). The cancel events are frequently overlooked, but any system acting on an A01 or A03 needs to receive A11 and A13 messages or its records will drift out of sync. ADT alerts vs. claims data for tracking patient transitions: which is better for value-based care? ADT alerts give you real-time visibility into admissions and discharges, often within minutes of the event. Claims data arrives weeks or months later, long after the window to intervene has closed, making ADT the only practical signal for preventing readmissions and capturing transitional care management billing. How do I know if my organization meets the CMS ADT notification requirements? CMS requires most Medicare-participating hospitals to send ADT notifications to a patient's treating clinicians at the time of admission or registration, and immediately prior to or at the time of discharge or transfer, with non-compliance risking loss of Medicare and Medicaid participation. If your hospital lacks a reliable outbound ADT feed connected to primary care providers and care teams, you are likely out of compliance with the rule that took effect in 2021. Why does ADT data alone often fall short for care coordination? ADT messages capture movement events and a diagnosis code, but typically lack deeper clinical context like lab results, vitals, or care plans, which limits how actionable the alert is by itself. Connecting an ADT notification to a patient's full longitudinal record (including discharge summaries and medication lists) turns an alert into something a care team can actually act on.

title: Trellus vs Salesfinity: Best AI Cold Calling Tools 2026

Key Takeaways from the Comparison For Real-Time Coaching Focus: Trellus.ai excels at providing live guidance during calls, making it ideal for teams that prioritize rep development and consistent messaging. The platform's AI coach listens to every call and delivers behavior suggestions in real-time, helping reps improve their conversational skills with each interaction. For Dialing Efficiency: Salesfinity's parallel dialing and contact enrichment capabilities make it the stronger choice for teams focused on maximizing dials per hour and connection rates. The platform's AI can handle up to 5 parallel dials simultaneously, enabling reps to have significantly more meaningful conversations per day. For Pricing Sensitivity: Trellus.ai offers more affordable entry points starting at $99.99/month for individuals, while Salesfinity's Silver plan begins at $200/user/month, making Trellus more accessible for smaller teams or solo SDRs exploring AI-powered cold calling. For Enterprise Features: Salesfinity's Enterprise plan includes dedicated customer success management, SSO/MFA, and advanced integrations like Gong and Slack, making it better suited for large organizations with complex requirements and multi-department workflows. Deep Dive into Trellus.ai Features: Why 8K+ SDRs Trust This Platform As the product owners of Trellus.ai, we're uniquely positioned to provide detailed insights into our platform's capabilities and evolution. Since our launch, we've onboarded more than 8,000 active users across diverse industries, and our platform maintains a 4.7-star rating on the Google Chrome Store . These metrics reflect not just adoption, but genuine user satisfaction and reliance on our platform for daily cold calling operations. Real-Time Call Coaching: Your AI Sales Coach on Every Call The cornerstone of Trellus.ai is our real-time call coaching engine. Unlike traditional sales coaching that happens after the call ends, our AI listens to every word of every conversation and provides live guidance to reps. This means when a rep is talking too fast, the AI suggests slowing down. When a rep is dominating the conversation, the AI prompts them to ask more questions. When a prospect raises an objection, the AI surfaces relevant counterarguments in real-time. This real-time intervention has proven transformative for sales teams. Reps report that the constant feedback loop accelerates their learning curve dramatically. New SDRs who might take months to develop conversational fluency can achieve competency in weeks with continuous AI coaching. The platform learns each rep's communication style and tailors suggestions accordingly, ensuring coaching feels personalized rather than robotic. The real-time coaching also creates consistency across your team. When every rep receives the same coaching on best practices, your entire team converges toward your organization's ideal sales methodology. This consistency translates directly to higher connection rates, more meetings booked, and shorter sales cycles. Objection Handling: AI-Powered Response Suggestions Objections are where most cold calls fall apart. A prospect says "we're not interested" or "we're locked into another vendor," and without a strong response, the call ends. Trellus.ai's objection handling system analyzes prospect statements in real-time and surfaces the most effective responses based on your team's historical win data and best practices. The system doesn't just suggest generic comebacks. Instead, it learns from your team's successful calls, identifying which objection responses lead to meetings booked or callbacks scheduled. Over time, the AI becomes increasingly intelligent about which responses work best for your specific industry, company size, and product type. This means your team's collective knowledge compounds, and newer reps benefit from the institutional wisdom of your top performers. The objection handling feature has been particularly valuable for new reps during their first 30-60 days. Rather than freezing when a prospect raises an objection, new reps can rely on AI suggestions to keep the conversation moving forward. This confidence boost accelerates ramp time and reduces early-career frustration. LinkedIn Superhuman Feature: Research and Personalization at Scale Cold calling without research is just noise. Trellus.ai's LinkedIn Superhuman feature transforms how reps prepare for calls. The tool automatically researches prospects on LinkedIn, identifying recent job changes, company announcements, content they've engaged with, and mutual connections. This research appears directly in the dialer interface, enabling reps to personalize their opening pitch in seconds. The efficiency gain is substantial. Rather than spending 5-10 minutes researching each prospect before dialing, reps have key talking points instantly available. This means more dials per hour, more personalized conversations, and higher connect rates. The feature integrates seamlessly with your existing sales engagement platform, whether that's Salesloft, Outreach, Apollo, or HubSpot. The LinkedIn Superhuman feature also reduces the friction of switching between tools. Reps don't need to open LinkedIn in a separate tab, search for the prospect, and then return to the dialer. Everything happens in one interface, keeping reps in flow state and maximizing their productivity. Parallel Dialing: Multi-Line Efficiency Without the Complexity Our Parallel plan enables reps to dial multiple numbers simultaneously, only connecting calls to the rep when a live person answers. This technology, borrowed from the telemarketing industry but refined for modern B2B sales, dramatically increases the number of meaningful conversations reps can have per day. Rather than waiting for each call to connect or ring out before dialing the next prospect, reps can have 3-5 calls in progress simultaneously. The platform's AI handles the initial connection and voicemail detection, passing only live conversations to the rep. This approach reduces wasted time on voicemails and disconnects while maintaining the personal touch that makes B2B cold calling effective. The parallel dialing feature is particularly valuable for teams working with large prospect lists or targeting high-volume markets. Reps can maintain their natural conversational style while dramatically increasing their throughput. The result is a significant boost in pipeline generation without requiring additional headcount. Conversational Intelligence and Call Analytics Every call on Trellus.ai is automatically transcribed and analyzed. The platform identifies key moments in the conversation—when objections were raised, when the prospect showed interest, when the rep asked effective questions. This conversational intelligence is then aggregated across your team to identify patterns. Sales managers can see which reps are booking the most meetings, which objections are most common, which opening statements resonate best, and which follow-up strategies convert prospects into opportunities. This data-driven approach to sales management replaces guesswork with evidence, enabling managers to coach reps on what actually works rather than what they think should work. The analytics dashboard also provides individual rep scorecards, showing each rep's performance against key metrics like connection rate, meeting booking rate, and average call duration. This transparency creates healthy accountability while also celebrating top performers and identifying reps who need additional support. Deep Dive into Salesfinity Features: A Balanced Perspective Salesfinity has earned its position as a market leader through relentless focus on dialing efficiency and team productivity. With 116 verified reviews on G2 and a 4.8-star rating , the platform has demonstrated consistent value delivery to its customer base. We recognize Salesfinity as a formidable competitor with genuine strengths that serve certain use cases exceptionally well. AI Parallel Dialer: 5.2x More Live Conversations Salesfinity's parallel dialing engine is engineered for maximum efficiency. The platform can simultaneously dial up to 5 numbers, intelligently routing live connections to available reps while automatically handling voicemails, disconnects, and invalid numbers. The result is a statistically significant increase in live conversations per rep per day. According to Salesfinity's case studies, teams using the parallel dialer achieve 5.2x more live conversations compared to traditional one-at-a-time dialing . For teams focused on volume and pipeline generation, this efficiency multiplier is transformative. The platform's AI voicemail detection has improved significantly, reducing the number of false positives that waste rep time. The parallel dialer also includes SmartRotate, which automatically rotates through your assigned phone numbers to maintain caller ID reputation and avoid spam flagging. This compliance-focused approach ensures your dialing remains effective even at high volumes. Nurture AI: Intelligent Follow-Up Automation One of Salesfinity's most innovative features is Nurture AI, which automatically analyzes call outcomes and schedules follow-ups at optimal times. When a prospect says "not now" or "call me back in three months," Nurture AI captures this intent and automatically schedules a callback at the precise moment when the prospect is most likely to be receptive. This automation eliminates the manual work of tracking follow-ups and ensures no opportunity slips through the cracks. For sales managers, it means their team's pipeline stays active without requiring constant manual intervention. The AI learns from your team's historical data to identify the best follow-up timing for different prospect segments and industries. Nurture AI also integrates with your CRM, automatically logging follow-up activities and updating prospect records. This creates a complete record of each prospect interaction, enabling managers to see the full lifecycle of each opportunity. Salesfloor: Team Collaboration and Live Coaching Salesfinity's Salesfloor feature brings remote teams together in a shared virtual space where managers can listen to live calls, provide whisper coaching, and create friendly competition through leaderboards and call challenges. This team-oriented approach to sales execution creates accountability and accelerates learning. The live coaching capability is particularly valuable for new rep onboarding. Rather than waiting for call recordings to review, managers can jump into live calls and guide reps in real-time. The competitive elements—leaderboards, call challenges, team goals—create engagement and motivation that traditional sales management approaches struggle to achieve. Salesfloor also enables peer learning. When top performers are on calls, other reps can listen in and learn from their techniques. This creates a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing. SmartGenie: AI Web Research Integration Salesfinity's SmartGenie feature automatically researches prospects using web data, company announcements, and intent signals. The research appears directly in the dialer interface, enabling reps to personalize conversations without manual research time. This is similar in concept to Trellus's LinkedIn Superhuman feature but draws from a broader range of data sources. SmartGenie also identifies buying signals and intent indicators, helping reps prioritize their outreach toward prospects who are actively in-market for solutions like yours. This targeted approach improves connection quality and increases the likelihood of meaningful conversations. Contact List Enrichment: 6+ Data Providers Salesfinity integrates with six or more data providers to continuously enrich contact lists in real-time. Invalid numbers are replaced with current contact information, ensuring your dialing list stays fresh and accurate. This data enrichment is particularly valuable for teams working with older prospect lists or targeting hard-to-reach decision-makers. The platform's waterfall enrichment approach tries multiple data sources in sequence, maximizing the likelihood of finding valid contact information. For teams that rely on high-volume dialing, having accurate, current contact data is essential to achieving target dials per rep. Advanced Reporting and Analytics Salesfinity's reporting dashboard provides comprehensive visibility into team performance. Managers can see individual rep scorecards, team trends, call quality metrics, and pipeline impact. The analytics go beyond simple call counts to reveal which reps are booking meetings, which are advancing deals, and which need coaching support. The platform's integration with CRM systems ensures that call outcomes are automatically logged, creating a complete record of each prospect interaction. This eliminates manual CRM updates and ensures data accuracy. The 360° Rep Profiles feature provides detailed performance metrics for each rep, enabling data-driven coaching and performance management. Pricing Transparency: Trellus.ai vs Salesfinity (2026 Rates) Understanding the true cost of ownership is critical when evaluating sales tools. Both Trellus.ai and Salesfinity offer transparent, tiered pricing, but their approaches differ significantly. Trellus.ai Pricing Structure Trellus.ai offers three pricing tiers designed to accommodate different team sizes and needs: Power Plan: $99.99/month (Individual focus) •Power dialing on all supported platforms •Voicemail drop capability •5 additional phone numbers with spam remediation •LinkedIn Superhuman feature •Suitable for solo SDRs or small teams Parallel Plan: $149.99/month (Individual focus) •Everything in Power plan, plus: •Multi-line parallel dialing •Unlimited AI practice calls •8 additional phone numbers with spam remediation •Ideal for high-volume individual contributors Business Plan: Custom pricing (Team focus) •Everything in Parallel plan, plus: •Customizable AI research and real-time coaching •Team-based analytics and conversational intelligence •Custom reporting and AI modeling •Dedicated support •Suitable for teams of 5+ reps Salesfinity Pricing Structure Salesfinity's pricing is per-user-per-month and scales with team size: Silver Plan: $200/user/month •Power dialer access •Single dialer access •5 assigned premium numbers •CallerID reputation management •Call recording and AI summaries •2-way CRM/SEP integration •LinkedIn integration •Reporting and analytics •Self-service support Gold Plan: $299/user/month •Everything in Silver, plus: •AI parallel dialer (up to 5 parallel dials) •Voicemail drop •10 assigned premium numbers •SmartRotate (automatic phone number rotation) •SmartGenie (AI web researcher) •BOSS Mode (team coaching) •Nurture AI (automatic follow-up scheduling) •API access Enterprise Plan: Custom pricing •Everything in Gold, plus: •Salesfloor access (team collaboration) •AI coaching and objection handling •AI training and advanced reporting •International dialing •Gong and Slack integration •SSO/MFA •Dedicated customer success manager Cost Comparison and ROI Analysis For a solo SDR or small team, Trellus.ai offers significantly better pricing. A single rep on Trellus's Parallel plan costs $149.99/month, compared to $200/month for Salesfinity's Silver plan. For a team of 10 reps, Trellus's Business plan (typically $1,500-2,000/month for 10 seats) compares favorably to Salesfinity's Gold plan at $2,990/month. However, Salesfinity's pricing includes more advanced features at lower tiers. The Gold plan's parallel dialer, Nurture AI, and SmartGenie are included at $299/month, whereas Trellus requires the Parallel plan ($149.99) plus a Business plan upgrade to access equivalent features. Both platforms report 4-month return on investment based on improved connect rates, meeting bookings, and reduced administrative time. The actual ROI depends heavily on your team's baseline performance and how effectively you implement the platform's features. For teams with 20+ reps, both platforms offer enterprise pricing that should be negotiated based on your specific requirements and usage patterns. Conclusion: Choosing the Right AI Cold Calling Platform The choice between Trellus.ai and Salesfinity ultimately depends on your team's primary objectives and constraints. Both platforms represent the state of the art in AI-powered cold calling, with strong user satisfaction, proven results, and continuous innovation. Choose Trellus.ai if your priorities are: •Real-time coaching and rep development •Affordable entry point for individuals or small teams •Seamless integration with your existing sales engagement platform •Focus on conversational quality over pure dial volume •Building institutional knowledge through conversational intelligence Choose Salesfinity if your priorities are: •Maximizing dials per rep and connection rates •Team collaboration and live coaching capabilities •Advanced contact enrichment and data quality •Comprehensive enterprise features and integrations •Nurture automation and intelligent follow-up scheduling The broader strategic insight is this: in 2026, cold calling success is no longer about dialing more numbers or having a better script. It's about leveraging AI to make every rep more effective, every conversation more personalized, and every team more data-driven. Whether you choose Trellus.ai or Salesfinity, you're investing in a platform that recognizes this reality and has built its product accordingly. The question isn't whether to use AI-powered cold calling tools—the market has clearly moved in that direction. The question is which platform aligns best with your team's culture, workflow, and growth objectives. Both Trellus.ai and Salesfinity are excellent choices; the right one for you depends on your specific needs, team size, and strategic priorities. Frequently Asked Questions 1. What is a Parallel Dialer? A parallel dialer is a technology that enables sales reps to dial multiple phone numbers simultaneously. Rather than waiting for each call to connect or ring out before dialing the next prospect, the dialer manages multiple calls in progress at once. When a live person answers, the call is routed to an available rep. Voicemails and disconnects are handled automatically. This approach significantly increases the number of meaningful conversations reps can have per day, often by 3-5x compared to traditional one-at-a-time dialing. Parallel dialers are particularly effective in high-volume sales environments where maximizing conversations per hour is critical to hitting pipeline targets. 2. How Does Trellus's Parallel Dialer Differ from Salesfinity's? Both platforms offer parallel dialing, but with different approaches and capabilities. Trellus's parallel dialer is designed to integrate directly into your existing sales engagement platform (Salesloft, Outreach, Apollo, etc.), providing a seamless experience within your current workflow. This integration-first approach means reps don't need to switch between tools. Salesfinity's parallel dialer is a more standalone feature that can dial up to 5 numbers simultaneously and includes advanced contact enrichment and voicemail detection. Trellus emphasizes integration and coaching, while Salesfinity emphasizes dialing efficiency and data quality. For teams already invested in a specific sales engagement platform, Trellus's approach may feel more natural. For teams looking for a comprehensive dialing solution, Salesfinity's feature set may be more compelling. 3. Why is Trellus.ai Better Suited for Professional B2B SaaS SDR Teams? Trellus.ai's real-time coaching engine and conversational intelligence are particularly valuable for B2B SaaS teams, where deal complexity and buyer sophistication require nuanced conversations. The platform's ability to provide real-time guidance during calls helps reps navigate complex objections and maintain consistent messaging. Additionally, Trellus's integration with modern sales engagement platforms makes it ideal for teams already using tools like Salesloft or Outreach, reducing implementation friction. The platform's focus on rep development and conversational quality aligns well with B2B SaaS sales culture, where building relationships and demonstrating expertise are critical to success. For teams where rep quality and consistency matter more than pure volume, Trellus.ai is the stronger choice. 4. Can Salesfinity and Trellus.ai Integrate with My CRM System? Yes, both platforms integrate with major CRM systems. Trellus.ai integrates with HubSpot, Salesforce, Outreach, Apollo, Amplemarket, and Zapier. Salesfinity integrates natively with HubSpot, Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft, Amplemarket, and Apollo. Both platforms automatically log call outcomes, transcriptions, and summaries to your CRM, eliminating manual data entry and ensuring your pipeline stays accurate. If you're using a CRM system not listed above, contact each platform's support team to discuss custom integration options. Most modern CRM systems can be connected via API or webhook, so integration is usually possible even if not pre-built. 5. How Does AI Objection Analysis Enhance Sales Calls? AI objection analysis works by listening to prospect statements during calls and identifying common objection patterns. The AI then surfaces relevant counterarguments, case studies, or talking points that have proven effective in similar situations. This real-time guidance helps reps respond to objections more effectively without needing to think on their feet. Over time, the AI learns which responses work best for your specific industry and product, making suggestions increasingly accurate and relevant. This capability significantly improves close rates and reduces the number of calls lost to unhandled objections. For new reps, AI objection analysis provides a safety net that builds confidence and accelerates learning. For experienced reps, it provides data-driven insights that improve their already-strong skills.

body_text: SALT LAKE CITY — July 21, 2026 — ReposiTrak, Inc. (NYSE: TRAK), the leader in retail supply chain, compliance and traceability solutions, today announced that the first warehouse-delivered supplier is live with a major retailer on ReposiTrak SBT 2.0. The implementation marks a significant expansion of the Scan-based Trading model beyond its traditional use by Direct Store Delivery suppliers. Under the new program, the supplier ships products through the retailer’s warehouse and distribution network while retaining ownership of the inventory until each product is scanned and sold at the retail register. “Scan-based Trading is not limited to suppliers delivering directly to stores,” said Randy Fields, chairman and CEO of ReposiTrak. “This successful launch demonstrates that the financial and operational benefits of SBT can also be extended to warehouse-delivered products. The retailer does not have to purchase and finance the inventory before it sells, while the supplier gains direct visibility into store-level sales and inventory movement.” ReposiTrak SBT 2.0 uses point-of-sale activity as the data of record for invoicing and inventory ownership. When a participating product is scanned at the register, the transaction automatically triggers the transfer of ownership from the supplier to the retailer and supports accurate supplier payment. The model provides benefits to both trading partners. The retailer reduces its investment in inventory and aligns payment with actual consumer sales. The supplier maintains ownership until the product sells while gaining access to store-level sales and inventory information that can support better forecasting, replenishment and product availability. Optional ordering assistance is also available through ReposiTrak for suppliers or retailers that need additional support managing replenishment. Ordering recommendations can use sales and inventory data to identify store-level product needs, reduce out-of-stocks and improve inventory productivity. “The ability to support warehouse-delivered products substantially expands the addressable market for SBT,” Fields added. “Retailers and suppliers can now evaluate SBT based on the economics of the product category and the trading relationship—not simply on whether the supplier delivers directly to the store.” About ReposiTrak ReposiTrak, Inc. (NYSE: TRAK) is an AI-powered, integrated platform that connects retailers, wholesalers, suppliers, and food manufacturers through a suite of applications designed to reduce risk, support regulatory compliance, strengthen operational controls, and protect brand integrity. The ReposiTrak platform serves as a shared system of record across its solution areas, maintaining and synchronizing complex supplier and customer data to enable secure, accurate, and scalable information exchange. ReposiTrak’s solutions are organized into three core product families: traceability, compliance and risk management, and supply chain solutions. Through its scalable, cloud-based platform and U.S.-based team of experts, the Company helps organizations streamline operations, improve data transparency, and meet evolving regulatory requirements across the food supply chain. For more information, visit repositrak.com . title: From rally to reality: credit markets enter a new phase
body_text: Despite geopolitical uncertainty, the broader macroeconomic environment continues to provide underlying support for credit markets, according to our credit strategy committee’s assessment. While stagflation risks persist – particularly in Europe – the US and many emerging market (EM) economies remain on relatively solid footing, underpinned by post-global financial crisis reforms and stronger policy discipline. Corporate fundamentals are similarly supportive. However, we have modest upward revisions to both macroeconomic and fundamental outlook scores, reflecting expectations that reduced geopolitical uncertainty could encourage renewed corporate investment and growth initiatives. Markets now appear to have begun to refocus on domestic fiscal and monetary policy considerations. Gilts rallied in late May in response to the falling oil price, but performance appears to have decoupled from the energy shock in recent weeks.

Automating Everything in a USB Cable Tester PCB Design
summary: Electrical engineer Cayden explores automating PCB design to address repetitive tasks using JITX, focusing on tasks such as pin connection, label generation, component placement, and autorouting.
body_text: ‍ TL;DR I’m Cayden, an electrical engineer and transhumanist hacker. In this article, I explore the frustrations of repetitive manual tasks in PCB design and the benefits of automation. I demonstrate the automation of tasks such as connecting pins, generating test points and indicator LEDs, programmatically placing components, and autorouting. Introduction If I’m writing a program, I’ll write a function one time, then use that function every time afterwards. Usually, if problems arise over and over again, we solve them once really well, then we don’t solve them again. Yet as an electrical engineer designing circuit boards, I often burn a lot of time on repetitive tasks. These tasks can get annoying - they’re something I’d rather automate. For example, to design a simple USB-C cable testing board I would have to: • Calculate and source a different current limiting resistor to get the desired brightness for every color of LED. • Type out, size, and place a custom text label that tells me what net each test point belongs to. • Redraw supporting circuitry from scratch every time I reuse a component in a new design. • Recheck datasheets many times as I connect various GPIOs and peripherals. It’s annoying to repeat tasks like this, and each piece of manual work carries a little risk of making a mistake. For my first design with JITX, I wanted to see how many of these pains I could automate away, and I wanted to know what design would feel like when I did. Electrical design shouldn’t be death by 1,000 paper cuts. Let’s automate the simplest board possible and see what that does for our experience as designers. You can see the full code and design files for this project in the JITX Cookbook: https://github.com/JITx-Inc/jitx-cookbook The Project A USB-C cable tester board tests every wire in a USB cable. It has two ports which connect to either end of the same cable. The board sends a voltage through each independent wire in the cable, through an indicator LED, and to ground. If the LED lights up - there is a connection. If it doesn’t light up - no connection. Indicator LED Schematic ‍ Bad USB cables cause headaches when doing board bring-up - I’ve personally spent hours debugging the UART on an embedded system only to find that the USB cable had a bad data connection. A USB cable tester can indicate the type and health of a USB cable, saving us from this pain. I’ve purposefully chosen a simple, easy design as I want to explore PCB design automation, and this will help me focus on trying to automate common, repetitive tasks. Automation TODO What can one automate here? I’ll try: 1. Connection of nets to the USB connectors. 2. Calculation of 18 LED ballast resistors given a desired color and brightness. 3. Naming all 18 test pads. 4. Placement Let’s do it. How? JITX EDA Tool in VS Code I’m going to use JITX to automate these tasks. JITX is a software defined electronics CAD tool. It’s similar to KiCad, Altium, and the other EDA packages, but instead of drawing PCBs, we define PCBs in code. That gives one the ability to turn manual tasks into code. Pin It To Win It - Connecting Pins Let’s create two USB connectors and a power net: net POWER (power) ... public inst in-usb : components/USB-C-1054500101/component public inst out-usb : components/USB-C-1054500101/component One side of the USB should be fully connected to our positive voltage rail. Instead of drawing a wire from every pin, let’s just connect them all at once: ; connect all pins of in-usb to power net (POWER pins(in-usb)) Test Points, Test Points Everywhere I’m going to create an indicator LED for every connection in the USB cable, so I’ll start with a text label and test point for each net. In the traditional EDA process, these are made and placed manually. I’ll automate it with a function that identifies the connected net and generates a silk screen label for the test point. This is a general helper function which I’ll write once now and expect to use over and over again in future designs. Below, I define a function which makes a test point and places a silk screen label with custom text: ; place a testpad defn my-testpoint-strap (tp:JITXObject, tp-name:String, diameter:Double) -> JITXObject: inside pcb-module : public inst tp-pad : gen-testpad(diameter) net (tp-pad.p tp) ; name the test point value-label(tp-pad) = Text(tp-name, 1.0, W, loc(1.2, 0.0)) inst my-label : ocdb/artwork/board-text/text(tp-name, 1.0, 0.0) place(my-label) at loc(1.2, -0.4, 0.0) on Top (relative-to tp-pad) tp-pad I can call this function in the above loop that generated the LEDs. I have now generated testpoints with custom silk screen labels. ; add a testpoint for this pin val test-pad = my-testpoint-strap(IN, net-name, 2.0) Next Generation LED Generation To test all the USB connections, the other USB connector must be split into separate nets. I’ll set up those nets: ; make nets for all of the pins on the usb C that we want to test for p in pins(out-usb) do : ; for each pin of the USB, we make a net make-net-from-pin-name(p) Each of these nets should then connect to an indicator LED. But first, to help with routing, I can order the nets based on their physical location. ; get all pins of the USB, and order them based on how they physically appear val ordered-pins = get-pins-physically-ordered(out-usb) ; convert from ordered list of pins to ordered list of nets val ordered-nets = map(get-named-net{self, _}, ordered-pins) Routes are made in order of pads' physical location. ‍ Routes are made in order of pads’ physical location. Now to generate an indicator LED for every USB pin. It’s a common issue for different LEDs on the same board to have vastly different brightnesses, like this: Uneven LED Brightness (Credit: SparkFun) ‍ To automate this common task and to make sure I don’t hit the common uneven LED brightness “gotcha”, I define a function called generate-test-led which takes in a color and an input voltage and uses those values to pick an LED and a suitable ballast resistor to achieve a nominal brightness. ; take a Tuple of pins we want to add status LEDs to, and the GND pin. Add status LEDs and test pins to each of the input pins. defn generate-test-leds-array (in-pins:Tuple, gnd-pin:JITXObject, voltage:Toleranced) : inside pcb-module : val colors:Seq = generate-rainbow(length(in-pins)) for (in-pin in in-pins, color in colors, place in 0 to false) do : ; create test LED and connect it inst test-led : generate-test-led(voltage, to-string(ref(in-pin)), color) net (in-pin test-led.in) net (gnd-pin test-led.out) ... ; generate an array of test LEDs for each net we just made generate-test-leds-array(ordered-nets, GND, property(battery.power.vdd.voltage)) ‍ Laziness Redefined - Programmatic Placement I now have 18 LEDs, 18 test points, and 18 ballast resistors. If I were to export now and open it in a legacy CAD tool, it’s just a big pile of components: Usually, the strategy now is to grab every component and manually drag them wherever we want. Or, one might use some basic alignment automation in existing CAD tools, but this still requires manual effort and time. Let’s do it better with automation. I can programmatically place components or submodules in code, which happens faster and works better than manual placement. In the for loop where I created the testpoints and LED modules, I can programmatically place anything I want on the board, with a bit of iterative arithmetic each time through the loop: val colors:Seq = generate-rainbow(length(in-pins)) for (in-pin in in-pins, color in colors, place in 0 to false) do : ; create test LED and connect it inst test-led : generate-test-led(voltage, to-string(ref(in-pin)), color) net (in-pin test-led.in) net (gnd-pin test-led.out) ; place components here ... Now everything is automatically placed. Better yet, if I change the LED type, test point size, board size, etc., it doesn’t matter, this will rerun to automatically yield the layout I want. Cheers to laziness! Routing in Your Sleep JITX has a built in autorouter, which automates a significant amount of the routing process. I can route most of this board in 30 seconds with a couple of clicks: ‍ Notice these autorouted traces look different than the traces on the physical board. In the first pass of this design, I manually routed everything in an external CAD tool. Afterwards, JITX released an autorouter, so I redid the routing with the autorouter, which is what you see above. Conclusion This is some very simple automation, but it does feel a bit magical to have the test points automatically created and properly named. The manual process of creating silk screen text and sliding it around in EDA board tools is always annoying, so I’m glad to have it automated away now and in the future. The LED generation module probably didn’t save me time yet , as I had to write it from scratch, which takes time, but now it exists forever, and I’m looking forward to reusing it many times in the future. It’s not all perfect though - one might notice that the LEDs on this board are bright . While all of the LEDs were the same brightness - they were all brighter than I’d want. I manually chose 50 mcd as the intensity, and this was way too high. An automation improvement would be to accept an enum of lighting options (e.g. nightime, indoor, outdoor) that could automatically choose the correct intensity for the application.

title: On Announces Strategic Additions to Global Leadership Team to Drive Consumer-Centricity
summary: ZURICH, Switzerland, July 7, 2026 – On Holding AG (NYSE: ONON), the Swiss sportswear brand renowned for its performance and innovation, today...
body_text: ZURICH, Switzerland, July 7, 2026 – On Holding AG (NYSE: ONON), the Swiss sportswear brand renowned for its performance and innovation, today announced two key appointments to its Leadership Team. Effective September 2026, the company is evolving its global commercial structure by splitting its commercial leadership into two distinct roles to further align with its long-term, consumer-centric ambitions. Rebecca Cai, currently General Manager of APAC, has been promoted to Chief Global Markets Officer , effective September 1, 2026. Alice Delahunt will join On as Chief Customer Officer , effective September 7, 2026. “We are thrilled to announce these two exciting leadership appointments, which are a direct reflection of our dedication to keep placing our consumer at the center of everything we do,” said Scott Maguire, President & COO at On. “As we grow our business and deliver the 'wow' to our fans worldwide, this new leadership set-up will enable greater focus and alignment.” Promoting from Within: Rebecca Cai named Chief Global Markets Officer As Chief Global Markets Officer, Rebecca Cai will lead On’s markets across the APAC, EMEA, and Americas regions, along with the Global Commercial teams. Cai will begin her transition on September 1, 2026 and will continue to lead the APAC team until a successor is identified, before relocating to Zurich next year. Since joining On six years ago, Cai has been a pivotal voice in the brand's growth journey. During her tenure as General Manager in APAC, the region's business grew six-fold. She brings outstanding leadership, deep commercial expertise, and an unwavering commitment to the team's culture. Elevating the Consumer Experience: Alice Delahunt named Chief Customer Officer Alice Delahunt brings a wealth of global leadership and entrepreneurial experience to her new role as Chief Customer Officer. Based in New York, Delahunt will oversee On’s Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) channels, spanning both Digital and Retail, as well as the brand's focus on Customer Loyalty. Delahunt joins On with a unique combination of brand, customer, digital, and business expertise. Her distinguished career includes senior leadership roles at Ralph Lauren and Burberry, board experience at Zalando, and entrepreneurial success as the founder of SYKY. “Alice and Rebecca will play a pivotal role in strengthening our ambition to become premium at every touchpoint alongside their world-class teams,” Scott Maguire added. “They will work closely with our Product, Marketing, and Supply Chain leadership to define what success looks like and further simplify our operating model.” The new commercial leadership structure follows the departure of Britt Olsen, who will leave by the end of September 2026, following a one-year transition period. "We are deeply grateful for Britt’s outstanding commitment and steady leadership over the past eleven years," said David Allemann, Founder and Co-CEO of On. "Her impact on our journey has been extraordinary – from playing an instrumental role in building our business in the Americas to establishing our first global Commercial function. We wish her the very best in her next chapter." About On On was born in the Swiss Alps in 2010 with the mission to ignite the human spirit through movement – a mission that still guides the brand today. Sixteen years after market launch, On delivers industry-disrupting innovation in premium footwear, apparel and accessories for high-performance running, outdoor, training, all-day activities and tennis. On’s award-winning CloudTec® and LightSpray™ innovation, purposeful design and groundbreaking strides within the circular economy have attracted a fast-growing global fan base – inspiring humans to explore, discover and Dream On. On is present in more than 80 countries globally and engages with a digital community on www.on.com .
